header.scope: Won: online membership billing only; front-desk studio processing is still with Global Payments, and phase two has no date.
header.incumbent: Global Payments (in place through the studio software; still processing at the front desk)
header.tag_why: The signature came four days after Tobi ran recovery analysis on the customer's own month of failed renewals and showed which declines usually come back with a retry or an updated card, which is decline performance proven in their own data rather than a general ROI case.

evidence.excerpt: They report member churn to the board every quarter, it had ticked up two quarters running
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: somebody finally split it into people who cancelled and people whose card just failed. The second bucket was a lot bigger than anyone expected.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: members who never meant to leave
evidence.label: quote

evidence.excerpt: I want to say a third of the churn? Don't quote me.
evidence.label: opinion

trigger.insight: This was a board-level churn problem, not a payments-provider shopping trip: the buying moment came when someone at the customer reframed failed cards as lost members. We have no reliable size for that bucket. The rep's 'a third' is self-disclaimed, and the real figure sits in a board deck we don't appear to have.
trigger.messaging: For subscription and membership businesses, open on involuntary churn in the customer's framing ('members who never meant to leave') and make M10 recovery the lead, not the M1 global opener.

evidence.excerpt: She said it was her call.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: The paper had gone to Greg and it sat with him for two weeks. Nothing.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: Yeah. His signature's on it.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: Maya chose us. Greg decided whether anybody got chosen.
evidence.label: opinion

decider.insight: The rep's first answer named the champion and left out the economic gate. Greg, the controller, held the paper for two weeks and signed it, and he only engaged once he saw numbers from his own data. Maya's claim that it was her call is relayed, not verbatim, and the rep's own account of the signature undercuts it.
decider.messaging: Give the controller a finance-ready artifact (recoverable revenue from their own failed-renewals file, plus a clear answer on contract term and exit cost) instead of relying on the head of digital to carry the case.

evidence.excerpt: What Maya told me is that they came back with a rate review and a new terminal bundle for the front desks, on a longer contract.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: Hardware. Suddenly everything was hardware. Before that meeting it was all failed payments and retries.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: what readers do you have, do they work inside our studio software, what's the contract term, what does it cost to get out
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: Greg asked about termination fees twice.
evidence.label: fact

competitor.insight: According to what Maya told the rep, the incumbent didn't fight on recovery. It moved the conversation to the front desk, where we depend on a partner, and to contract lock-in. After that meeting the customer stopped asking about our strength and started asking about our gap. It is unclear whose termination fees Greg was asking about, and whether the front desks took the longer Global contract. That second point matters for phase two. 'Rattled' is only the rep's read.
competitor.messaging: Expect the incumbent to counter with hardware and contract terms, and come prepared with a front-desk answer and a plain statement of our term and exit cost, rather than letting the deal reset onto readers.

evidence.excerpt: Tobi, took an export of one month of their failed renewals and showed which ones were the kind that usually come back with a retry or an updated card. Their file, not our average.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: Greg hadn't said a word in two meetings, and he asked for the spreadsheet.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: Silence. I opened with the global slide. They have studios in the US and a handful in Canada.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: is that the readers?
evidence.label: quote

message.insight: Our two lead claims missed. M1's 'grow globally, in every currency' fell flat with a customer in the US and a handful of studios in Canada. M3's 'unified commerce' was heard as hardware, the one area where we couldn't deliver. What landed was M10 made concrete on their own file, and the rep's own phrase 'not our average' is a direct rebuke of average-uplift claims like M4.
message.messaging: Replace average-based proof (M4, M6) with a standard 'your failed renewals, analysed' session, and stop using 'unified commerce' as a label without saying what it concretely means at their front desk.

evidence.excerpt: When Greg asked for the spreadsheet.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: Before that I honestly thought we were there to keep the incumbent honest.
evidence.label: opinion

evidence.excerpt: The paper had gone to Greg and it sat with him for two weeks. Nothing.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: Then we did the data session, and four days later it was signed.
evidence.label: fact

decided.insight: The rep thought we were there to keep the incumbent honest until the data session. A two-week stall at finance ended four days after that session. The data session was not a closing tactic. It was the only thing that moved the person who signed, and it came late, after the paper was already stuck.
decided.messaging: Position the own-data recovery analysis as an early, standard evaluation step aimed at finance ('see what your failed renewals are worth'), not a rescue move once the contract stalls.

evidence.excerpt: They asked to see our reader working inside their studio management software.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: We couldn't show that live. It runs through a partner integration, and the partner did a call the week after.
evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: the studio managers will revolt.
evidence.label: quote

evidence.excerpt: Not yet. It depends on the partner piece.
evidence.label: fact

gaps.insight: The gap didn't lose the deal, but it is why this is half a win. The customer only saw the partner's demo, not their own setup, the front desk is still on Global, and phase two has no date because it depends on the partner. M3's claim that the online/in-store line 'has pretty much disappeared' was disproven in this deal by Maya's own fear that staff would end up with two screens.
gaps.messaging: Until we can show our reader live inside the customer's studio software, describe in-store as a partner integration with a named path, and don't claim single-platform parity in M3 for front-desk-heavy businesses.

Note that the three quotes cited in the language section surfaced in other answers, not in reply to this question.

gaps.question: How big was the failed-card bucket?
gaps.follow_up: Ask the rep to get the actual figure from Maya's board deck, or ask Maya directly, and don't use 'a third' in the meantime.

gaps.question: Who made the final call?

gaps.follow_up: Ask the rep whether Greg's two termination-fee questions were about leaving Global, about our contract, or both.

gaps.follow_up: Ask the rep (via Maya) whether the studios signed the counteroffer, and if so, when that term ends relative to phase two.

gaps.follow_up: Ask the rep and the partner team what has to be delivered for the reader to run inside the customer's studio software, and who owns the date.

close.rep_takeaway: Your strongest move was Tobi's session on the customer's own failed renewals, so run it before the paper goes to finance, not after it stalls for two weeks. And when someone asks who decided, name the person who signs, not just the person you talked to most.
